title: Riya Patel
text:
Welcome! I am a data analyst pursuing an M.S. in Biomedical and Health Informatics at Case Western Reserve University. I have more than two years of experience working with SQL, Excel, and financial and business data, and I hold an MBA and an M.S. in Information Systems from Cleveland State University.
Right now, I work as a Data Entry Specialist at LP Tax & Accounting, where I verify client financial and tax data and am building a centralized database for the firm’s 800+ business and personal tax clients. In my graduate program, I am learning biostatistics and reproducible research with R and Quarto. I am especially interested in clinical electronic health record (EHR) systems and the data they generate: how it is captured, structured, and used to support care and research.
I am currently looking for an internship or part-time research opportunity in health informatics, and I am also open to data analytics roles, ideally in the Cleveland area. If your team works in this space, I would welcome the chance to connect.

title: Projects
text:
Centralized Client Database (LP Tax & Accounting)
2026 – Present | Microsoft Access, SQL, database design
I am building a centralized database in Microsoft Access and SQL that brings together records for more than 800 business and personal tax clients, giving the team one organized place to access client information. This database is an essential foundation for the firm’s next project: integrating AI tools into its accounting workspace.


Business Development Call Analysis (OneThirtyFive)
Fall 2025 | Qualitative analysis, presentation
I reviewed recorded business development calls, identified patterns across them, and turned my findings into recommendations for the marketing and sales teams.


Natural Language Processing in Python
Python, TextBlob, NLTK, Tweepy, pandas, matplotlib
In a Jupyter notebook, I worked through core natural language processing techniques: tokenization, part-of-speech tagging, sentiment analysis with both TextBlob’s default analyzer and a Naive Bayes classifier, language detection and translation, spell checking, and lemmatization. I analyzed word frequencies in Romeo and Juliet and visualized the most common words with a bar chart and a word cloud. I also used the Twitter API to collect and search live tweets, automatically translating non-English tweets into English.
View the notebook on GitHub
